dedupe_keys.name: galveston testbed multi hazard socio physical datasets for coastal community resilience

description: The Galveston Testbed provides datasets and companion code for assessing the hurricane resilience of Galveston Island, Texas, covering its built, natural and social systems. It was established by the NIST Community Resilience Center of Excellence and published on DesignSafe-CI by Kooshan Amini, Jamie Padgett, Tanmoy Palit, Abigail Beck, Jayant Patil, Tao Lu, Himadri Sen Gupta and Yousef Darestani, with an entry-point report for the paper 'Integrated Decision-Support Framework for Enhancing Coastal Community Resilience Against Hurricane-Induced Hazards' (Amini et al., 2025). Six collections hold the paper code, a residential building inventory, multi-hazard intensity fields (ADCIRC+SWAN storm fields, FEMA flood-depth rasters and a LiDAR DEM), the transportation network with mainland bridges, tract-level social vulnerability data, and a distribution-level electric power network. Coverage: Galveston Island. Access: DesignSafe Data Depot, project PRJ-4527, with code on GitHub. Licence: Open Data Commons Attribution; free. Caveats: the README files hold the attribute details, which were not read here. Simulation uses: multi-hazard damage, loss, population dislocation, recovery and mitigation optimisation for coastal communities. Related records: the Onslow Community Resilience Testbed and IN-CORE.
